name: Maya Chen
story: Building Loam, a startup that turns food waste into fertilizer. Born in Taipei, raised partly in Vancouver. Hosts a monthly dumpling night in Bed-Stuy and is the person who somehow knows everyone.

todos.text: Visit the Red Hook farm where Loam is piloting
Bring a dessert to the November dumpling night
Send her the pottery studio link

moments.title: Fourth dumpling night
moments.text: Fourth dumpling night at her place. Zara played cello for an hour in the living room, Yusuf brought cold brew. Maya announced Loam has its first paying farm customer.

moments.title: Walk along the waterfront
moments.transcript: Walked from Red Hook to the ferry. She is nervous about hiring her first engineer and does not want to hire a friend. I said hire the best person and keep the friend.

moments.title: Her birthday dinner
moments.text: Birthday dinner at a Taiwanese place in Sunset Park, twelve people at one round table. Gave her a handmade bowl from Hannah’s studio.

moments.title: Met at Climate Week
moments.transcript: Met Maya Chen at Climate Week, we got stuck in the same line for coffee. She is a founder, Loam, turns food waste into fertilizer. Born in Taipei, lives in Brooklyn. Super warm, invited me to her dumpling night.

name: Daniel Okafor
story: Designs at a fintech in the Mission and runs a monthly sketch club at a bar on Valencia. Collects old film cameras and has opinions about every one. Grew up in Lagos.

todos.text: Go to the October sketch club
Ask him which film camera to buy first

moments.title: Sketch club night
moments.transcript: Drew strangers at the bar for two hours. He lent me a Pentax and showed me how to load the film. Terrible photos, great evening.

moments.title: Design crit on my portfolio
moments.text: He tore through my portfolio in a kind way. Cut half the case studies, lead with the one that has numbers.

moments.title: Met at Config
moments.transcript: Met Daniel Okafor at Config, he gave the best talk on design critique. Product designer in San Francisco, grew up in Lagos. Runs a sketch club and collects film cameras. Said I should come drink and draw.

name: Sofía Ramírez
story: Recruits for startups in Austin and is training for her first marathon in December. Loves spicy food and keeps a ranked list of every taco truck she has tried.

todos.text: Ask how the marathon training is going
Send her my résumé notes before she does a search for me

moments.title: Call about her training plan
moments.transcript: Twenty miles on Sunday, knee a bit sore. She wants a running partner for the long Saturday runs if I am ever in town.

moments.title: Met at SXSW
moments.transcript: Met Sofía Ramírez at SXSW, a recruiter based in Austin. From Mexico City. She is running her first marathon and had strong views on tacos. Offered to review my resume anytime.

name: Liam O'Connor
story: Moved to Berlin for a robotics job after we graduated. Plays upright bass in a jazz trio that gigs in Neukölln. Still sends me terrible Irish memes at 2am.

todos.text: Visit Berlin and see the trio play
Reply to his meme about the ferry

moments.title: Christmas Eve call
moments.transcript: Called him from the airport. He is not coming home this year because of a robot demo. The trio got a residency at a bar, every second Thursday.

moments.title: Visited him in Berlin
moments.text: Stayed on his couch for four days. Saw the trio play in a basement, then ate döner at 1am on a bridge.

moments.title: Met at Study abroad
moments.transcript: Met Liam O’Connor on the first day of our semester in Copenhagen, he lived across the hall. Software engineer, from Dublin, plays bass. We stayed up until four talking about nothing.

name: Aisha Khan
story: Invests in health and hardware startups. Just adopted a corgi named Toast and now every meeting starts with a photo. Grew up in Karachi, went to school in Boston.

todos.text: Ask her who funds early battery companies
Meet Toast at the dog run

moments.title: Lunch near Bryant Park
moments.transcript: She explained how seed investors think about hardware margins. Showed me forty photos of Toast. Offered to look at any deck I send.

moments.title: Drinks after the health panel
moments.text: Met her colleague Rohan, who invests in fintech. She introduced half the room to the other half.

moments.title: Met at Demo Day
moments.transcript: Met Aisha Khan at Demo Day, she was on the investor panel. VC associate, invests in health and hardware. Sharp questions, very funny afterwards. From Karachi.

name: Kenji Watanabe
story: Opening a ramen counter in Shimokitazawa next spring. Promised me a tasting before the menu is final. Obsessed with baseball and will explain the infield fly rule unprompted.

todos.text: Book flights for the ramen counter tasting

moments.title: Video call from the empty shop
moments.transcript: He walked me through the bare space, the counter has twelve seats. Still deciding between two broths and wants my honest vote.

moments.title: Ramen crawl in Shinjuku
moments.text: Four bowls in one night with his chef friends. He rated each one out of ten, loudly.

moments.title: Met at Friend’s dinner
moments.transcript: Met Kenji Watanabe at a friend’s dinner in Tokyo, he cooked the whole thing. Chef, from Osaka. Opening his own ramen counter. We talked about baseball for three hours.

name: Priya Nair
story: Builds wildfire prediction models for a climate nonprofit. Big board game fan and hosts game nights in Oakland. Moved from Bangalore for grad school and stayed.

todos.text: Ask about the battery data set she mentioned
Bring a new game to her game night

moments.title: Game night in Oakland
moments.transcript: Played Wingspan and a very long round of Codenames. She is publishing her wildfire model open source next month.

moments.title: Coffee about career moves
moments.text: She is deciding between staying at the nonprofit or joining a startup. I said ask which one lets her ship models faster.

moments.title: Met at Climate meetup
moments.transcript: Met Priya Nair at a climate meetup in San Francisco. Data scientist, wildfire models, lives in Oakland. She is the person to ask about battery and grid data. Invited me to game night.

name: Tom Becker
story: Writes about cities and transit for a London magazine. Bikes everywhere, including to the airport. Hamburg native with a dry sense of humor.

todos.text: Send him the article about the bus lanes
Ask if he needs a source in New York

moments.title: Call about his transit piece
moments.transcript: He is writing about congestion pricing and wanted to know how it feels from the New York side. Quoted me in one line.

moments.title: Met at Conference
moments.transcript: Met Tom Becker at a conference in London, he writes about cities and transit. From Hamburg. Cycled to the venue in the rain and was the only dry one. Easy to talk to.

name: Grace Kim
story: Roommate from freshman year. Wants to specialize in pediatrics and is on her rotations in Boston. Goes to every Red Sox home game she can and hikes the Blue Hills on rare free weekends.

todos.text: Go to a Red Sox game when she is next off
Ask how the pediatrics rotation went

moments.title: Fourth of July in Boston
moments.transcript: Watched the fireworks from the Esplanade with her and Nina. She matched her first choice for the next rotation.

moments.title: Fenway opening weekend
moments.text: Cold, lost, and she cried during the anthem a little. Bought her a hot chocolate.

moments.title: Study session care package
moments.text: Dropped off soup and flashcards before her boards. She texted a photo of the empty bowl.

moments.title: Met at College
moments.transcript: Met Grace Kim, we got assigned as freshman roommates. Med student in Boston, from Seoul. She labeled everything in our fridge. We have been close ever since.

name: Lucas Silva
story: Hosts a Sunday supper club in Lisbon for people new to the city, forty at a long table on a rooftop. Born in São Paulo and talks about food as the fastest way to belong.

todos.text: Cook for his supper club if I visit
Send him my grandmother’s feijoada recipe

moments.title: Video call about the supper club
moments.transcript: They hit one hundred dinners. He wants to turn it into a nonprofit and asked how I would set up the board.

moments.title: Met at Web Summit
moments.transcript: Met Lucas Silva at Web Summit, he runs a supper club for newcomers in Lisbon. From São Paulo. Handed me an invite on the back of a napkin. Very generous energy.

name: Hannah Cohen
story: Specializes in incorporations and seed rounds. Offered to look over our incorporation docs for free. Throws pots on weekends at a studio in Gowanus and sells mugs at a fall market.

todos.text: Buy a mug at her fall market

moments.title: Review of the incorporation docs
moments.transcript: She marked up the docs in green pen, flagged the vesting clause. Told me to never skip the 83(b) filing.

moments.title: Pottery studio visit
moments.text: Tried the wheel for an hour and made a lopsided cup. She glazed it for me in a color called “wet moss”.

moments.title: Met at Founder dinner
moments.transcript: Met Hannah Cohen at a founder dinner, she is a startup lawyer. From Chicago, lives in Manhattan. She said she loves helping early founders and also, randomly, pottery.

name: Omar Haddad
story: Designs passive houses and renovates old Parisian apartments. Just got back from hiking Patagonia and cannot stop talking about the wind. Grew up in Beirut.

todos.text: Ask him for the Patagonia trail names
Share the passive house article with him

moments.title: Photos from Patagonia
moments.transcript: He showed me the whole trek on his phone, nine days, one blister. Wants to organize a group trip next year.

moments.title: Met at Mutual friend
moments.transcript: Met Omar Haddad in Paris through a mutual friend. Architect, designs passive houses, from Beirut. We walked three hours through the Marais while he pointed out building details.

name: Emma Wright
story: Teaches middle school science in Melbourne. Childhood best friend, her family spent two years in Naperville before moving home to Sydney. Runs a book club that has read the same thriller four times by accident.

todos.text: Call her on her birthday in March
Send her the book about volcanoes for her class

moments.title: Long overdue call
moments.transcript: Two hours on the phone. She is applying to be head of department and is scared. I told her she has run the whole school for years anyway.

moments.title: Summer in Melbourne
moments.text: Beach day, then her book club, which had a screaming match over the ending. We left with three borrowed novels.

moments.title: Met at Elementary school
moments.transcript: Emma Wright, my best friend since fifth grade in Naperville, when her family moved there for two years. She sat next to me and shared her pencils on the first day. Now she is a science teacher in Melbourne.

name: Noah Patel
story: Thinking about leaving his job to start a newsletter on how small brands grow. Big baseball fan and has a Blue Jays season ticket he rarely uses. Grew up in the suburbs of Toronto.

todos.text: Ask if he wants to split a Jays game

moments.title: Call about quitting
moments.transcript: He has six months of savings and one subscriber. I said launch with a tiny weekly issue before you leave.

moments.title: Met at Collision
moments.transcript: Met Noah Patel at Collision in Toronto. Growth marketer, thinking about starting a newsletter. Huge baseball guy. He explained funnels using a hot dog stand.

name: Ana Ruiz
story: Ex-Tesla battery engineer who now consults for early startups. Wants to advise early founders and is generous with her time. Runs along the Hudson at 6am and has done three marathons.

todos.text: Ask her about cell sourcing for a founder I met
Join a Saturday run along the Hudson

moments.title: Run and breakfast
moments.transcript: Ran five miles, ate eggs on a bench by the pier. She said the biggest mistake founders make is ordering parts too early.

moments.title: Office hours for a friend
moments.text: Took a founder friend to her office hours. She spent an hour on thermal management and refused payment.

moments.title: Met at Founder dinner
moments.transcript: Met Ana Ruiz at the same founder dinner as Hannah. Hardware engineer, used to work on batteries at Tesla. Says she wants to advise early founders. Runs along the Hudson every morning.

name: Jordan Smith
story: Cooks tasting menus on weeknights and hosts a Sunday supper club for friends. Grew up in Chicago and still defends the deep dish. Has not been in touch in a long time.

todos.text: Reach out and ask about the next supper club

moments.title: January supper
moments.text: Eight courses, one strangely perfect carrot dish. Promised to stay in touch and then did not.

moments.title: Met at Supper club
moments.transcript: Met Jordan Smith at a supper club in the East Village, the guy cooking. Chef from Chicago. Fed twelve strangers a seven course meal in a tiny kitchen.

name: Zara Ahmed
story: Plays cello and produces ambient music, with a show in November at a gallery in Bushwick. Just got into bouldering and talks about her first V2 like a championship.

todos.text: Take her bouldering when she asks

moments.title: Rehearsal for the November show
moments.transcript: Sat in on the rehearsal. Layered cello loops, a field recording of rain in Nairobi. She wants me to say honestly if the middle section drags.

moments.title: First time at the climbing gym
moments.text: She sent a photo after her first V2, face covered in chalk. Asked if I know anyone who wants to climb on weeknights.

moments.title: Met at Gallery opening
moments.transcript: Met Zara Ahmed at a gallery opening in Brooklyn, she played a live set with her cello. Musician, from Nairobi. Told me she just got into bouldering.

name: Marcus Bell
story: Runs the Thursday night pickleball league at the Prospect Park courts and keeps the ladder rankings in a spreadsheet nobody else may edit. Former college tennis player, now a physical therapist. Always short one player and always happy to take a beginner.

todos.text: Bring my own paddle on Thursday
Ask him about the winter indoor league

moments.title: Thursday league night
moments.transcript: Won two games and lost four. He taught me the dink and fixed my grip. The after-game beers turned into dinner.

moments.title: Summer tournament
moments.text: His team took second in the borough doubles tournament. He was mad about a single net call for a week.

moments.title: Ladder night
moments.text: First time in the league. Marcus wrote my name at the bottom of the spreadsheet with a smiley face.

moments.title: Met at Pickleball league
moments.transcript: Met Marcus Bell at the pickleball courts in Prospect Park, he runs the Thursday league. Physical therapist from Atlanta. Handed me a loaner paddle and put me on the beginner ladder.

name: Dana Reyes
story: Played Division I tennis and now coaches kids at a public court in Queens on weekends. Also plays in the Thursday pickleball league for fun and beats most people. Fiercely competitive and weirdly gracious about it.

todos.text: Ask her to help with my backhand
Go watch her kids’ tournament in November

moments.title: Hit with her in Queens
moments.transcript: An hour of tennis rallies at her court. She said I am overthinking my footwork. We got tacos after.

moments.title: Met at Pickleball league
moments.transcript: Met Dana Reyes at the pickleball league, she destroyed me twice and then fixed my serve. Tennis coach from Houston, lives in Queens. Very kind about the whole thing.

name: Theo Park
story: Builds chairs and tables out of reclaimed wood in a shared workshop in Gowanus. Shares a studio wall with a ceramics class, which is how he knows Hannah. Quiet, funny, and takes six months to finish anything he cares about.

todos.text: Commission a small bench for the hallway

moments.title: Visited the workshop
moments.transcript: Watched him cut dovetails by hand. He is finishing a dining table for a restaurant and has already redone the legs twice.

moments.title: Dinner with the studio crowd
moments.text: Hannah, Mia and Theo talked glazes versus oils for an hour while I ate everyone’s leftovers.

moments.title: Met at Studio open house
moments.transcript: Met Theo Park at a studio open house in Gowanus, he builds furniture from reclaimed wood. From Los Angeles. He let me sand one edge of a table and called it “a team effort”.

name: Nina Volkov
story: College friend finishing a postdoc on memory and sleep. Lives on cold brew and spreadsheets and sings in a community choir on Tuesdays. Remembers every birthday, which is a little ironic.

todos.text: Hear her paper presentation in December
Send her the sleep podcast I mentioned

moments.title: Fireworks with Grace
moments.transcript: Nina was on call so she showed up late with ice cream. She is on the job market for a faculty position and is trying not to talk about it.

moments.title: Met at College
moments.transcript: Met Nina Volkov in the dining hall freshman fall, she was reading a neuroscience textbook for fun. From Chicago. We became study partners immediately.

name: Rachel Lin
story: My cousin, the one who is basically a sister. Pediatric nurse in Seattle, works nights, and is the funniest person at every family dinner. Training for a half marathon with her two dogs.

todos.text: Visit in February when the dogs are in their winter coats

moments.title: Sunday call
moments.transcript: She is tired from three night shifts but the half marathon is on track. Told me about a kid who made her a card with a drawing of a dog and a stethoscope.

moments.title: Visited Seattle
moments.text: Walked the dogs along Alki Beach and ate fish and chips. She is considering a move into the NICU.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Rachel is my cousin, we grew up spending every summer together. She is a pediatric nurse in Seattle and my favorite person to call at midnight.

name: Aunt Mei Lin
story: My aunt, who runs a Taiwanese bakery in Flushing and has since 2004. Wakes at 3am, sends pineapple cakes whenever someone is sad, and tells everyone I am too thin. Rachel’s mom.

todos.text: Help at the bakery on Lunar New Year
Learn how she makes the milk bread

moments.title: Sunday at the bakery
moments.transcript: Helped pack mooncake boxes for the festival. She slipped me a bag of egg tarts for the train and refused payment for anything.

moments.title: Her 60th birthday
moments.text: Surprise party in the bakery after closing. She cried, then asked who was going to clean up.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Aunt Mei, my mom’s older sister. She taught me to fold dumplings when I was six and still criticizes my pleats.

name: Andre Lin
story: My younger brother, a junior studying computer science at UCLA. Plays intramural soccer and is secretly the best cook in the family. Calls only when he needs something and then stays for an hour.

todos.text: Send him a care package before midterms

moments.title: Late-night call
moments.transcript: He got an internship offer and does not know whether to take it. We went through pros and cons until he fell asleep on the phone.

moments.title: Visited him in LA
moments.text: Soccer match, then he cooked a three-course dinner on a two-burner stove. I did the dishes.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Andre is my brother, born when I was eight. I held him the day he came home and was terrified of dropping him.

name: Ben Adler
story: Fractional CFO for four seed-stage companies in Chicago. Explains cash runway with a coffee-and-sugar analogy and means it. Plays league volleyball and runs a spreadsheet for his own life.

todos.text: Ask him for a budget template for Loam-style startups
Send him my cap table questions

moments.title: Call about budgeting
moments.transcript: He built me a three-scenario forecast in an hour. Rule of thumb: raise when you have eighteen months of runway, not six.

moments.title: Met at Founders breakfast
moments.transcript: Met Ben Adler at a founders breakfast in Chicago, he is a fractional CFO. Very practical. Drew my startup’s runway on a napkin in under a minute.

name: Camila Torres
story: Product manager at a digital health company in New York. Writes the clearest specs I have read and keeps a running list of books she lends and never gets back. Weekend painter.

todos.text: Ask for the product spec template
See her paintings at the open studio

moments.title: Lunch about product career paths
moments.transcript: She said PM is mostly saying no kindly and writing it down. Gave me two books and wrote her name inside both.

moments.title: Met at Product meetup
moments.transcript: Met Camila Torres at a product meetup in New York. PM at a digital health company, from Buenos Aires. She asked the one question that made the whole panel rethink.

name: Yusuf Demir
story: Roasts small-batch coffee in a Greenpoint warehouse and sells to eleven cafés. Left a corporate job at a bank and has not regretted it once. Makes the best cold brew and brings it to every party.

todos.text: Buy a bag of the new Ethiopian roast
Help him pack orders on a Saturday

moments.title: Dumpling night again
moments.transcript: He brought a new Ethiopian cold brew. We argued about whether light roasts are overrated. Winner: nobody.

moments.title: Tour of the roastery
moments.text: Smelled like toast and fruit. He let me pull the sample from the drum and I burned my thumb.

moments.title: Met at Dumpling night
moments.transcript: Met Yusuf Demir at Maya’s dumpling night, he arrived with a huge jug of cold brew. Coffee roaster in Greenpoint, German-Turkish. Very funny, a bit shy at first.

name: Inès Moreau
story: Runs a tiny natural wine bar in the 11th arrondissement and knows every grower by first name. Studied law and quit after a year. Talks about wine like it is gossip about people she loves.

todos.text: Visit the bar next time I am in Paris
Ask her to recommend a wine for a gift

moments.title: Evening at the bar
moments.transcript: Twelve seats, no menu, she chooses. Sat next to a stranger who turned out to be a friend of Omar’s too. Paris is small.

moments.title: Met at Mutual friend
moments.transcript: Met Inès Moreau in Paris, introduced by Omar. She owns a natural wine bar. Poured me five glasses and made me guess the grapes. I got one right.

name: Felix Wagner
story: Runs a bike repair collective in Berlin and rides a cargo bike with a dog named Brezel in the front box. Friend of Liam’s, met at one of the trio’s gigs. Believes every problem can be fixed with a hex key.

todos.text: Ride with him when I visit Berlin
Ask for help picking a commuter bike

moments.title: Call about bikes
moments.transcript: He talked me through a flat tire over video. His dog barked through the whole thing.

moments.title: Met at Jazz gig
moments.transcript: Met Felix Wagner at Liam’s jazz gig in Neukölln. He runs a bike repair collective, brought his dog in a cargo bike. We talked about brake pads for an hour and I enjoyed it.

name: Amara Osei
story: Directing a documentary about street food vendors in Accra and Brooklyn. Shoots on a borrowed camera and edits at the library because the Wi-Fi is better. Friend of Zara’s who invited me to a screening.

todos.text: Help her find a Brooklyn vendor to interview
Go to the rough-cut screening in December

moments.title: Rough cut viewing
moments.transcript: Watched forty minutes. The Accra scenes sing; the Brooklyn ones feel rushed. She wrote everything I said in a notebook.

moments.title: Shoot day in Sunset Park
moments.text: Held a boom pole for a vendor interview. The vendor made us eat before we could film anything.

moments.title: Met at Screening
moments.transcript: Met Amara Osei at a short film screening in Brooklyn, she directed one of the films. From Accra. She asked what I thought and actually listened to the answer.

name: Victor Huang
story: Research quant at a trading firm, which he describes as “a very expensive way to guess”. Hosts a monthly board game night with scorecards and a trophy. Plays pickleball when someone drags him.

todos.text: Bring a new game to his board game night
Ask him to explain options pricing once more

moments.title: Game night finale
moments.transcript: He won the season trophy by a single point. Gave a speech. We then played one more round of Catan at 1am.

moments.title: Met at Game night
moments.transcript: Met Victor Huang at a board game night in the East Village, he brought a custom scoreboard. Quant researcher, from Taipei. Competitive but the best loser.

name: Lila Sharma
story: Emergency room nurse in Philadelphia and my neighbor from the old apartment. Teaches a free Sunday yoga class in the park and knows all the neighborhood cats by name. Calm in a crisis, chaotic with parking.

todos.text: Join her Sunday yoga when I am in Philly
Send photos of my new plant for advice

moments.title: Phone call about her night shifts
moments.transcript: She is cutting down to three nights a week. Yoga class has twenty regulars now. Asked me to come in spring.

moments.title: Met at Apartment building
moments.transcript: Met Lila Sharma in my first sublet on the Lower East Side, she lived next door and fed my cat when I was locked out of town. ER nurse, from Mumbai. Instant friend.

name: Rohan Mehta
story: Founder of a payments startup for small restaurants, just closed a seed round. Met through Aisha. Sleeps four hours a night and still remembers everyone’s kids’ names.

todos.text: Introduce him to a restaurant owner I know
Ask how the hiring is going

moments.title: Call after his seed round
moments.transcript: He raised four million. First hires: a head of sales and an ops lead. Wants advice on pricing for tiny restaurants.

moments.title: Met at Founder drinks
moments.transcript: Met Rohan Mehta at founder drinks in San Francisco, introduced by Aisha. He runs a payments startup for restaurants. Funny, sleep deprived, very generous with intros.

name: Sasha Ivanova
story: Runs user interviews for a mapping company in Berkeley and knits scarves through every meeting. Moved from Saint Petersburg ten years ago. Can read a room faster than anyone I know.

moments.title: Coffee in Berkeley
moments.transcript: She gave me her interview script and a half-finished green scarf as a joke. Said the best insight comes at the end, when they relax.

moments.title: Met at Design meetup
moments.transcript: Met Sasha Ivanova at a design meetup in Berkeley, she was knitting during the talk. UX researcher. Told me the secret to good interviews is waiting five seconds after they stop talking.

name: Caleb Foster
story: Guides multi-day hiking and ski trips in the Colorado Rockies and tells stories about close calls with perfect calm. Hosts a gear swap every spring. Lives in a van half the year.

todos.text: Join his September trip to the Maroon Bells
Borrow his ice axe for the winter trip

moments.title: Weekend in the Rockies
moments.transcript: Three days, forty miles, one thunderstorm. He pointed out a pika and never once checked the map.

moments.title: Ski day at Loveland
moments.text: He taught me how to read snow and made me carry the shovel. Best day of the year.

moments.title: Met at Friend’s wedding
moments.transcript: Met Caleb Foster at a friend’s wedding in Denver, he was the only person in hiking boots. Backcountry guide, lives in a van. We sat at the same table and talked about the stars.

name: Mia Tanaka
story: Illustrates children’s books from a sunny studio in Portland and draws tiny comics on napkins. Shares a ceramics shelf with Theo’s studio friends. Her next book is about a bear who learns to knit.

todos.text: Order a print of the bear comic
Ask for a portfolio review tips

moments.title: Studio visit in Portland
moments.transcript: She showed me her new bear book in pencil. Put me in a cameo as the tired owl again.

moments.title: Met at Art fair
moments.transcript: Met Mia Tanaka at an art fair in Portland, she was drawing the crowd in tiny panels. Illustrator, from Tokyo. She drew me as a tired owl and signed it.

name: Owen Murphy
story: Does stand-up at open mics in Austin and bartends to pay rent. Tests material on anyone who stays still. Sofía introduced us after a taco crawl.

todos.text: Send him a joke about airport pickleball

moments.title: Show at the open mic
moments.transcript: Ten minutes about moving, landlords and his mother. The mother joke killed. Bought him a drink.

moments.title: Met at Taco crawl
moments.transcript: Met Owen Murphy on a taco crawl with Sofía in Austin. Stand-up comedian, bartends, from Boston. He roasted every taco and then ate all of them.

name: Elena Rossi
story: Teaches urban planning at a New York university and researches how streets shape neighborhoods. Walks everywhere with a notebook. Friend of Tom’s from the London conference.

todos.text: Send her the bus lane article
Attend her public lecture in November

moments.title: Office hours chat
moments.transcript: She showed me maps of how walking routes changed after a bus lane opened. Invited me to guest in her class.

moments.title: Met at Panel discussion
moments.transcript: Met Elena Rossi on a panel about streets and neighborhoods. Urban planning professor, from Milan. She said a good street is one where you forget you are walking.

name: Jamal Washington
story: Teaches history and coaches the junior varsity basketball team at a public school in Atlanta. Has taken every team to the playoffs and apologizes for none of it. Plays Sunday pickup at the Y.

todos.text: Watch a game when I am in Atlanta
Send him a book on the civil rights movement for his class

moments.title: Phone call before playoffs
moments.transcript: His team made the second round. He had a whole speech planned and then said nothing, just handed out oranges.

moments.title: Met at Alumni weekend
moments.transcript: Met Jamal Washington at alumni weekend in Atlanta, he teaches history and coaches basketball. Big laugh, big handshake. He said every kid needs one adult who is on time.

name: Anika Rao
story: Policy analyst in Washington who turns research into bills staffers can actually read. Friend of Maya’s, met at a climate happy hour. Bakes sourdough for the whole office and keeps the starter on her desk.

todos.text: Ask her for the summary of the grid bill

moments.title: Call about the grid bill
moments.transcript: She walked me through which parts will pass. Her tip: follow the appropriations, not the speeches.

moments.title: Met at Climate happy hour
moments.transcript: Met Anika Rao at a climate happy hour in Washington, she is a policy analyst. From Bangalore. She explained a whole bill to me in three sentences and then gave me bread.

name: Sophie Laurent
story: Physiotherapist in Vancouver who runs ultras on weekends and volunteers at the aid stations when she is injured. Met through Noah’s newsletter community. Carries salt tablets and a sense of humor.

todos.text: Pace her on a long run if I visit
Ask her about stretching for runners

moments.title: Call about her 50K
moments.transcript: She finished her fifty kilometers in nine hours. Said she cried at mile thirty-five and then ate a pickle.

moments.title: Met at Trail race
moments.transcript: Met Sophie Laurent at a trail race in Vancouver, she was volunteering at the aid station and handed me a banana. Physiotherapist, runs ultras. Funny and very organized.

name: Kwame Boateng
story: Backend engineer at a mobile payments company in Accra and a mentor for young coders on weekends. Friend of Amara’s and the one who first showed her around Accra. Plays highlife on guitar.

todos.text: Ask about mentoring programs I could help with
Learn a highlife song from him

moments.title: Video call about mentoring
moments.transcript: He runs a free coding class for forty teenagers. Wants volunteers for a Saturday workshop.

moments.title: Met at Tech meetup
moments.transcript: Met Kwame Boateng at a tech meetup in Accra, he is a backend engineer and mentor. Kind, quick, plays guitar. He explained mobile payments with a market story.

name: Olivia Grant
story: Edits literary fiction at a New York publisher and runs a book club that drinks more wine than it reads. Annotates everything in three colors. Believes the best sentence in any book is the last one.

todos.text: Read the novel she is editing
Bring a friend to her book club

moments.title: Book club night
moments.transcript: We read a short story collection. Eight people, four bottles, one very heated argument about the last story.

moments.title: Coffee about my writing
moments.text: She read my essay and said the opening paragraph is the real start. Cut everything before it.

moments.title: Met at Book launch
moments.transcript: Met Olivia Grant at a book launch in Manhattan, she edits fiction. From Boston. She handed me three book recommendations in two minutes and got every one right.

name: Arjun Kapoor
story: Anesthesiologist in Houston who plays tabla and organizes a charity concert every Diwali. College roommate of a friend. Never sleeps on schedule and says it is part of the job.

todos.text: Go to the Diwali concert this year

moments.title: Call about the charity concert
moments.transcript: Last year raised twenty thousand for a free clinic. He is booking a bigger hall this time.

moments.title: Met at Diwali concert
moments.transcript: Met Arjun Kapoor at a Diwali concert in Houston, he played tabla. Anesthesiologist, from Mumbai. He told me every concert is a rehearsal for the next one.

name: Tessa Nguyen
story: Photographs weddings and restaurants in Los Angeles and shoots film on her own time. Took the best portrait anyone has ever taken of me by accident. Terrible at texting back, great at turning up.

todos.text: Develop the film roll she gave me

moments.title: LA visit and photo walk
moments.transcript: Walked Venice at golden hour while she shot two rolls of film. She made me promise to send her a print of the best one.

moments.title: Met at Friend’s wedding
moments.transcript: Met Tessa Nguyen at a friend’s wedding in LA, she was the photographer and the only one who knew everyone’s names. Shoots film on the side. Very warm and fast.

name: Gabe Silverman
story: Principal of a public elementary school in Brooklyn and an unrepentant dad-joke collector. Plays Thursday pickleball with Marcus and walks to work with a thermos. Knows every child’s name and every parent’s excuse.

todos.text: Volunteer for the school’s book fair

moments.title: League night
moments.transcript: We paired up for doubles and lost to two teenagers. He said that is how you know they are well taught.

moments.title: Met at Pickleball league
moments.transcript: Met Gabe Silverman at the Thursday pickleball league. He is a principal in Brooklyn, from Philadelphia. He told a dad joke at every changeover and still won.

name: Nora Lindqvist
story: Researches soft robots at a university lab in Copenhagen and works with Liam on a joint project. Swedish, dry sense of humor, and keeps a drawer full of tiny prototypes. Bakes cardamom buns when an experiment fails.

todos.text: Ask for a lab tour next time I am in Copenhagen

moments.title: Video call about the project
moments.transcript: The new gripper handles eggs. She said the paper is rejected twice and she is celebrating with buns.

moments.title: Met at Robotics conference
moments.transcript: Met Nora Lindqvist at a robotics conference in Berlin, Liam introduced us. Researches soft robots in Copenhagen. She showed me a gripper that picks up a grape without breaking it.

name: Santiago Ortiz
story: Founded a neighborhood food delivery app in Mexico City that pays couriers weekly. Plays five-a-side soccer every Wednesday and brings orange slices. Introduced through Sofía at SXSW.

moments.title: Call about scaling
moments.transcript: They hit fifty thousand orders a month. He is nervous about expanding to a second city and wants an honest second opinion.

moments.title: Met at SXSW
moments.transcript: Met Santiago Ortiz at SXSW, a friend of Sofía’s. He runs a food delivery app in Mexico City. Passionate about paying couriers fairly and equally passionate about soccer.

name: Hana Yoshida
story: Makes tableware for restaurants from a kiln studio in Tokyo and supplies Kenji’s ramen counter with the bowls. Talks about glaze the way other people talk about family. Shy until she starts talking about clay.

todos.text: Buy a set of her bowls
See the kiln when I visit Tokyo

moments.title: Kiln visit with Kenji
moments.transcript: Watched a firing at midnight. She pulled the first bowl out of the kiln and cried a little, then covered it up with a joke.

moments.title: Met at Friend’s dinner
moments.transcript: Met Hana Yoshida at the same dinner as Kenji, she made all the bowls. Ceramic artist in Tokyo. Told me the best bowl is the one you forget you are holding.

name: David Lin
profession: Electrical engineer at a national lab
story: Dad. Came to Illinois from Taipei for grad school and never left. Retiring in June and already planning raised garden beds.

todos.text: Help him plan the garden beds at Thanksgiving

moments.title: Sunday call
moments.transcript: He is retiring in June. Wants to learn to bake bread and build raised beds. Asked if I am still eating vegetables.

moments.title: Home for the Fourth
moments.text: Riverwalk fireworks with everyone. He grilled far too much and handed the leftovers to the neighbors.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Dad, obviously. Taught me to fix a bike and to be ten minutes early to everything.

name: Susan Lin
story: Mom. Works four days a week at a dental office and sings in the church choir. Sends a photo of whatever she cooked, every night, whether or not I asked.

todos.text: Learn her pork dumpling recipe at Thanksgiving
Send her a photo of the apartment

moments.title: Video call
moments.transcript: She showed me the new kitchen tiles for twenty minutes. Asked if the Bushwick place has a real oven.

moments.title: Birthday dinner
moments.text: Took her to a restaurant in Chinatown. She critiqued the dumplings and then ordered a second plate.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Mom. She taught me to read before kindergarten and to never leave a party without thanking the host.

name: Po Po (Chen Mei-Hua)
story: Mom's mother, lives with my parents. Sewed half the family's clothes and still hems everything I own. Plays mahjong on Thursdays and takes it very seriously.

todos.text: Bring the torn blazer to have her fix it

moments.title: Visit home
moments.transcript: She re-hemmed three pairs of pants without being asked and sent me back with a bag of oranges.

moments.title: New Year dinner
moments.text: She won at mahjong against my uncle and would not stop mentioning it.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Po Po. She measured me for my first winter coat when I was four.

name: Yeh Yeh (Lin Chi-Ming)
story: Dad's father, 88, lives in Taipei and does calligraphy every morning. We talk on video every other Sunday, in my bad Mandarin and his patient English.

todos.text: Learn to write my own name in calligraphy

moments.title: Sunday video call
moments.transcript: He showed me the character he practiced all week. Told me that patience is the only real secret to a good brush stroke.

moments.title: Visited Taipei
moments.text: Two weeks with him. We walked every morning to the same tea stall and he corrected my tones in public.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Yeh Yeh. The first time I met him I was three months old, apparently, and cried until he gave me tea.

name: Uncle Frank Wu
story: Aunt Mei's husband. Retired from the transit authority and now fixes whatever breaks at the bakery. Takes the family fishing off Long Island every July.

todos.text: Ask him to look at the Subaru noise

moments.title: Mooncake Sunday
moments.transcript: Helped him carry flour sacks at the bakery. He told me about the 1990s subway signals for an hour.

moments.title: Fishing trip
moments.text: Caught one fish, he caught eleven. He insisted I take the cooler home.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Uncle Frank, Aunt Mei's husband. Quiet until you mention anything with an engine.

name: Kevin Wu
story: Cousin, Aunt Mei's son, a year older than me. Works at a logistics company and lives in Jersey City, one PATH stop from half my friends. Plays pickup basketball on Sundays.

todos.text: Play pickup basketball in Jersey City

moments.title: Dinner in Jersey City
moments.transcript: Ramen near his place, then he showed me the game he is building on weekends. Asked me to design the icons.

moments.title: Wedding weekend
moments.text: We sat at the kids table even though we are in our late twenties and ate all the almond cookies.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Kevin, my cousin. We were each other's only friend at every family party until I was twelve.

name: Tina Chen
story: Cousin on Mom's side, a pharmacist in Seattle. Hikes every weekend the weather allows and bakes bread when it does not. Rachel's roommate for two years.

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: She is thinking about going part time to study for an advanced pharmacy certificate. Sent me a photo of a very good loaf.

moments.title: Seattle visit
moments.text: Dinner with her and Rachel on the water. Talked about whether our grandparents' generation ever had time off.

moments.title: Met at Family
moments.transcript: Tina, my cousin on Mom's side. She taught me to swim in a hotel pool.

name: Coach Dale Brandt
profession: History teacher and cross country coach
story: My cross country coach and history teacher at Naperville Central. Believes any problem can be solved with a long easy run. Still writes me a postcard every New Year.

todos.text: Visit him next time I am in Naperville

moments.title: Coffee when I was home
moments.transcript: He is retiring after 31 years. Asked me to speak at the senior banquet and I said yes before thinking.

moments.title: Turkey trot
moments.text: Ran the five miles together. He still has the stopwatch from my best race.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Coach Brandt, the cross country coach. First day of summer practice: eight miles, no talking.

name: Walter Ostrowski
story: My sophomore and senior English teacher. Handed me a book of design essays and said I should stop pretending I wanted to be an engineer. Retired and writing a memoir about the Cubs.

todos.text: Thank him in the speech at the banquet

moments.title: Lunch at the old diner
moments.transcript: He read me two pages of the memoir. Wants to know if I would draw the cover.

moments.title: Graduation party
moments.text: He gave me a used copy of the design essays and a note. I still have both.

moments.title: Met at Sophomore English
moments.transcript: Mr. Ostrowski, English. He wrote 'go draw something' on the back of my essay.

name: Maddie Kowalczyk
story: Ran next to me for four years of cross country. Now an ICU nurse in Chicago who has done three marathons and counts all of them as warm-ups. Still texts a group chat of the old varsity girls and boys.

todos.text: Run the Chicago marathon cheering spot with her
Send her the old team photo

moments.title: Visited Chicago
moments.transcript: Brunch, then a lakefront walk. She is switching to night shifts and says it has ruined her social life but fixed her sleep.

moments.title: Chicago marathon
moments.text: Stood at mile 18 with a sign. She waved and gave me a thumbs down as a joke.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Maddie, the girl who passed me in the last mile at the first meet and said sorry.

name: Ravi Subramanian
story: Ran the two-mile with me and cracked jokes through every mile. Works at a trading firm in the Loop and runs a Wednesday trivia night. Brought me my first real espresso at fifteen.

todos.text: Go to his Wednesday trivia night
Ask what he does all day

moments.title: Trivia night
moments.transcript: Our team came second thanks to a question about the Chicago Cubs that I actually knew. He demanded a rematch.

moments.title: Holiday drinks
moments.text: Everyone from the old team in one bar. We argued about who really won the sectional in 2014.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Ravi, the funniest runner on the team. Also the slowest to stop talking.

name: Tyler Hobbs
story: My best friend on the cross country team. Left Illinois for Colorado at 18 and never looked back. Guides trail runs in the summer and patrols a ski hill in winter.

todos.text: Visit him in Denver in September
Send him the photo from the 2014 regional

moments.title: Phone call from the trail
moments.transcript: He called from a ridge with no signal, which is why it cut out three times. Wants me to run a hundred miler with him someday. I said no, politely.

moments.title: Colorado ski trip
moments.text: Four days on his couch. He taught me to ski moguls badly.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Tyler, the tall guy who did the whole workout in basketball shorts and shared his orange slices.

name: Anjali Desai
story: Captain of the high school robotics club when I was a skeptical designer on the team. Now doing a PhD on robot navigation in Pittsburgh. Still beats everyone at board games.

moments.title: Video call
moments.transcript: She is two chapters from the finish. Asked me to be on the call when she practices her defense.

moments.title: Friend's wedding
moments.text: Danced to the same song three times. She cried when the class robot came up in the toast.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Anjali, robotics captain. She made me draw the team logo and then used it for four years.

name: Sam Whitfield
story: My lab partner on the robotics team. Now a software engineer in Seattle. We trade terrible puns and he still owes me a sandwich from a bet in 2013.

moments.title: Game night over video
moments.transcript: Four hours of a co-op game. He cooked dinner on camera and burned it.

moments.title: Seattle trip
moments.text: Ate chowder on the pier. He admitted he never actually liked robotics, just us.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Sam, the one who solders with the radio on. Said my sketches made the robot look friendly.

name: Leah Brenner
story: My first love, senior year. We broke up politely before college and we stayed kind to each other. Now an occupational therapist in Minneapolis with a very fat cat.

todos.text: Send her a New Year text

moments.title: New Year text
moments.transcript: We caught up for an hour. She is engaged. I was genuinely happy and slightly stunned at how easy it felt.

moments.title: Coffee in Naperville
moments.text: First time we talked in a year. We laughed about prom for twenty minutes.

moments.title: Met at Prom
moments.transcript: Leah. We met when she borrowed a pen in chemistry. Neither of us gave it back.

name: Gus Papadakis
story: Worked the register next to me at the bookstore on Washington Street all through high school. Now owns a small bookshop in Madison and writes terrible, wonderful poetry.

moments.title: Visited Madison
moments.transcript: Helped him shelve a new delivery. He gave me a signed chapbook of poems about customer returns.

moments.title: Naperville holiday
moments.text: He ran into me at the old bookstore, which closed that fall. We stood in the empty shop.

moments.title: Met at Bookstore job
moments.transcript: Gus, my coworker at the bookstore. Gave me the discount on a used art book the first week.

name: Mikey Russo
story: The kid next door. We built forts, broke a window with a baseball, and shared a bus stop for ten years. Now an electrician who runs his own small crew.

todos.text: Grab beers when I am home
Help him with a logo for his van

moments.title: Backyard fourth
moments.transcript: He grilled for both our families and told me about the time he wired a whole restaurant in a weekend.

moments.title: Holiday visit
moments.text: He asked what I actually do and I showed him on my phone. He said it looks like paperwork.

moments.title: Met at Next door
moments.transcript: Mikey, the neighbor. He let me hold his pet turtle on day one.

name: Priscilla Okonkwo
story: My best friend from middle school, in the same lunch table until she moved to Atlanta. We reconnected when she moved to Astoria two years ago. Runs strategy at a branding agency and organizes the loudest brunch in the neighborhood.

todos.text: Help her pick a name for her side project

moments.title: Astoria brunch
moments.transcript: Four hours at a table by the window. She is thinking about leaving her agency to go freelance.

moments.title: She moved to Astoria
moments.text: Helped her carry boxes up four flights. She paid me in dumplings.

moments.title: Met at Middle school
moments.transcript: Priscilla, my best friend from seventh grade. She told me my haircut looked fine, which was a lie and a kindness.

name: Ethan Cho
story: Youth group friend, played bass in the worst band in Naperville with me on drums for one summer. Now a product manager in Austin and a very patient father of twins.

todos.text: Call when the twins are asleep
Send him the old band recording

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: He showed me a photo of the twins in matching dinosaur pajamas. Said fatherhood is mostly logistics.

moments.title: Reunion barbecue
moments.text: We tried to play one song and gave up after the second verse.

moments.title: Met at Youth group
moments.transcript: Ethan from youth group. Cannot keep a beat, will not stop trying.

name: Karen Halvorsen
story: Taught me piano from age eight to fifteen and was kinder than I deserved. Retired from teaching but still hosts a student recital every May in her living room.

todos.text: Go to the May recital next year

moments.title: Annual recital
moments.transcript: I played one short piece badly and she clapped like I was a professional. Her cat was in the front row.

moments.title: Visited her house
moments.text: She still had my first lesson book with the gold star sticker.

moments.title: Met at Piano lessons
moments.transcript: Mrs. Halvorsen, piano. Her cat sat on the bench during every lesson.

name: Jonah Feld
story: Cabin mates at a summer camp in Wisconsin, eight summers in a row. He moved to Brooklyn two years before I did and slept on my sublet floor on my first weekend.

todos.text: Come to his rough cut screening

moments.title: Rough cut screening
moments.transcript: Watched the first cut of his film about a retiring lock maker in Sunset Park. I cried at the key scene.

moments.title: My first weekend in New York
moments.text: He slept on the floor of the sublet and showed me where to get a bagel at midnight.

moments.title: Met at Summer camp
moments.transcript: Jonah, the cabin mate who learned all the camp songs ironically and then sincerely.

name: Hailey Brooks
story: Babysat me and my brother on Friday nights and made up elaborate board games. Now a school counselor in Pilsen who paints murals on weekends.

todos.text: Look at her new mural in Pilsen

moments.title: Coffee in Pilsen
moments.transcript: She walked me past her mural of a woman holding a school bus. It took her four months.

moments.title: Naperville fair
moments.text: She remembered the board game down to the rules.

moments.title: Met at Babysitter
moments.transcript: Hailey, the babysitter who let us stay up if we finished the game she invented.

name: Wendy Tsai
story: My parents' best friends' daughter, so basically a sister. Tax accountant at a mid-size firm and does my taxes every March for free and a box of mooncakes. Lives in Jersey City.

todos.text: Send her my receipts by March

moments.title: Dinner in Jersey City
moments.transcript: Dumplings and a long talk about her trying to buy a one-bedroom. She explained mortgage points with a napkin.

moments.title: Taxes
moments.text: She finished my return in an hour and told me I should keep better records. I promised and did not.

moments.title: Met at Family friend
moments.transcript: Wendy, our families' kid. She taught me how to fold a dumpling properly and judged my first attempt.

name: Kofi Mensah
profession: Mechanical engineer at a medical device company
story: My rival at every middle school science fair and then my friend. Became a mechanical engineer making medical devices in Boston. Still plays Sunday soccer in a league for people who used to be good.

todos.text: Ask him about the devices he works on

moments.title: Video call
moments.transcript: He told me about a prototype he is proud of and could not say what it did. Asked if I would help with the icons on its screen.

moments.title: Boston weekend
moments.text: Sunday soccer in the cold, then ramen. He still scored most goals.

moments.title: Met at Middle school science fair
moments.transcript: Kofi, the other kid with a volcano at the science fair. His erupted better.

name: Sana Qureshi
story: We were each other's only non-Chinese-speaking classmate at the Saturday Chinese school, where we both failed spectacularly. Now a pediatrician in Houston with two golden retrievers.

todos.text: Congratulate her on the practice opening

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: She opened her own pediatric practice last month. Showed me the waiting room mural on video.

moments.title: Winter break
moments.text: We tried to remember the characters from Saturday school and managed four.

moments.title: Met at Chinese school
moments.transcript: Sana, the girl at Chinese school who did not speak Chinese either. We shared notes in English.

name: Marcus Ellison
story: Second chair next to me in the middle school band. Plays the saxophone better than anyone should. Now a public defender in Brooklyn and moonlights in a jazz quartet that plays Tuesdays in Fort Greene.

todos.text: Hear the quartet on a Tuesday
Ask for advice on the lease

moments.title: Jazz night in Fort Greene
moments.transcript: His quartet played an hour-long set. He dedicated a ballad to the middle school band director.

moments.title: Lunch
moments.text: He walked me through my rights as a tenant after the landlord tried to keep the deposit.

moments.title: Met at Middle school band
moments.transcript: Marcus, the saxophone. Held the whole section together and never took credit.

name: Bridget O'Neill
story: Sat behind me in third grade and now treats half the dogs in town. Still names every stray she meets.

todos.text: Bring the dog for a checkup

moments.title: Backyard barbecue
moments.text: She brought a rescue puppy and handed him to me within a minute.

moments.title: Holiday visit
moments.text: Coffee at the diner, she told me about her first surgery on a hawk.

moments.title: Met at Elementary school
moments.transcript: Bridget, third grade. She lent me a purple pencil and never asked for it back.

name: Raymond Zhou
story: Saturday Chinese school classmate who ran the ping pong table in the basement. Took over his uncle's orthodontics practice.

todos.text: Play ping pong at his place

moments.title: Ping pong rematch
moments.text: I lost again but scored four points, a personal record.

moments.title: Thanksgiving weekend
moments.text: He fixed my night guard and refused payment.

moments.title: Met at Chinese school
moments.transcript: Raymond, from Chinese school. He beat me at ping pong eleven times in a row.

name: Amy Castellanos
story: Lived two doors down and ran the neighborhood lemonade stand. Teaches second grade in the district she grew up in.

todos.text: Send her a drawing for her classroom

moments.title: Block party
moments.text: She organized the whole cul-de-sac and put me on the cooler.

moments.title: Fourth of July
moments.text: Her class sent me a thank-you card with a drawing of my face. Accurate.

moments.title: Met at Neighborhood
moments.transcript: Amy, down the block. We split the lemonade profits unevenly.

name: Jerome Baptiste
story: Middle school locker neighbor and the first friend who made me laugh in class. Treats college athletes in Atlanta.

moments.title: Phone call
moments.text: He diagnosed my ankle over video and was annoyingly right.

moments.title: Reunion lunch
moments.text: We recited the principal impression in unison.

moments.title: Met at Middle school
moments.transcript: Jerome, locker 212. Spent seventh grade doing impressions of our principal.

name: Meera Iyer
story: Danced at every school talent show and still does at weddings. Practices pediatric dentistry in Houston.

moments.title: Holiday text thread
moments.text: A forty-message thread about a cousin's wedding dance.

moments.title: Graduation party
moments.text: She led the whole room through a choreographed number.

moments.title: Met at Middle school
moments.transcript: Meera, seventh grade. She taught me the one dance move I know.

name: Colin Murphy
story: Played catcher on my Little League team and now coaches one. Inspects buildings and is deeply serious about fire exits.

moments.title: Little League game
moments.text: I sat on his bench and kept the scorebook badly.

moments.title: Beers on the porch
moments.text: He explained why every candle I own is a hazard.

moments.title: Met at Little League
moments.transcript: Colin, Little League catcher. He told me where to stand in right field.

name: Noelia Vasquez
story: Spanish class partner who made me practice out loud. Court interpreter in Chicago now and dances cumbia on weekends.

moments.title: Lunch in Pilsen
moments.text: We spoke Spanish for an hour and I only panicked twice.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: She taught me to say my own job in Spanish.

moments.title: Met at Spanish class
moments.transcript: Noelia, Spanish class. She said my accent was a crime and fixed it.

name: Greta Hoffman
story: The children's librarian who handed me my first graphic novel. Runs the summer reading program and still remembers my card number.

moments.title: Library visit
moments.text: She showed me the shelf she keeps for kids who don't like reading yet.

moments.title: Holiday visit
moments.text: Dropped off a donated art book. She put a sticker with my name in it.

moments.title: Met at Public library
moments.transcript: Ms. Hoffman, the library. She said I should try something with pictures.

name: Tommy Nguyen
story: His parents ran the pho place by the train station. He runs it now, with the same broth and a new patio.

moments.title: Sunday lunch
moments.text: He put me at the family table and refused the check.

moments.title: Reopening
moments.text: First dinner service after the lockdown. We all cried a little.

moments.title: Met at Neighborhood
moments.transcript: Tommy, from the pho place. Free spring rolls came with every report card.

name: Dana Whitaker
story: Camp counselor who led the canoe trips. Now a middle school principal and still carries a whistle.

moments.title: Coffee
moments.text: She told me about the hardest kid she ever got through to.

moments.title: Camp reunion call
moments.text: Eight of us singing the camp song badly over video.

moments.title: Met at Summer camp
moments.transcript: Dana, counselor at camp. She counted heads every five minutes.

name: Xavier Pierce
story: Played trumpet in the middle school band and now produces a public radio show. Records everything on his phone.

moments.title: Studio tour
moments.text: He showed me the booth where he cuts tape for hours.

moments.title: Dinner
moments.text: He interviewed me for a story about moving cities. It aired as thirty seconds.

moments.title: Met at Middle school band
moments.transcript: Xavier, trumpet. He recorded my audition and played it back to me, cruelly.

name: Liliana Ortega
story: My babysitter's little sister, who grew up to be a doctor. Delivers babies in Dallas and sends photos of the funny ones.

moments.title: Phone call
moments.text: She is on call for three nights straight and still cooked.

moments.title: Visit home
moments.text: She is the only one who remembers I used to play the recorder.

moments.title: Met at Neighborhood
moments.transcript: Liliana, the neighbor's kid. I taught her to ride a bike.

name: Peter Szymanski
story: Mikey's cousin who spent summers on our street. Wires buildings and plays accordion at weddings.

moments.title: Wedding band
moments.text: He played polka until the dance floor wore out.

moments.title: Lake day
moments.text: He caught the only fish and named it after me.

moments.title: Met at Neighborhood
moments.transcript: Peter, Mikey's cousin. He showed up with an accordion. Nobody asked.

name: Yasmin Nasser
story: Debate partner in eighth grade who always argued the other side. Immigration attorney in Chicago.

todos.text: Ask her about a friend's visa

moments.title: Phone call
moments.text: She walked a friend of mine through a visa timeline in ten minutes.

moments.title: Lunch
moments.text: We debated whether pineapple belongs on pizza. She won.

moments.title: Met at Middle school
moments.transcript: Yasmin, debate. She won every round by being nicer.

name: Calvin Reed
story: Rode bikes with me every summer and now runs a corner bakery. Gets up at 3am without complaining.

moments.title: Bakery visit
moments.text: He gave me a warm loaf and a stool behind the counter.

moments.title: Holiday rush
moments.text: I packed boxes for two hours and went home with flour in my hair.

moments.title: Met at Neighborhood
moments.transcript: Calvin, summer bike gang. He crashed into a mailbox with style.

name: Shira Katz
story: Camp friend who led the singing. Now a rabbi in Evanston who officiated a friend's wedding with jokes.

moments.title: Wedding officiant
moments.text: She made a hundred strangers laugh and cry in ten minutes.

moments.title: Coffee
moments.text: She told me about the weight of eulogies.

moments.title: Met at Summer camp
moments.transcript: Shira, bunk neighbor. She wrote the camp song everyone still sings.

name: Owen Fitzgerald
story: Ran two-mile with me and now teaches math at our old school. Assistant coach for the cross country team.

moments.title: Team practice
moments.text: I paced the freshmen for a mile and nearly died.

moments.title: Halloween run
moments.text: We ran in costumes. He was a calculus textbook.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Owen, the quiet runner. Said his first word to me at mile two.

name: Hannah Berg
story: Sat next to me in art class and made better pots than the teacher. Now has a pottery studio in Minneapolis.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: She showed me the kiln opening. Forty mugs, thirty-nine perfect.

moments.title: Graduation exhibit
moments.text: Her pot beat mine in the senior show. Fair.

moments.title: Met at Art class
moments.transcript: Hannah, art class. She fixed my cracked bowl and never mentioned it.

name: Devon Clarke
story: Robotics teammate who designed the drivetrain. Builds boat engines in Seattle and sails when the weather lets him.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: He showed me a diesel engine he assembled in a shed.

moments.title: Seattle trip
moments.text: He took me out on his sailboat and let me hold the rope.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Devon, drivetrain guy. He measured twice and still blamed me.

name: Elise Park
story: Choreographed the school musical I painted sets for. Now choreographs small shows in Brooklyn and teaches on weekends.

moments.title: Her showcase
moments.text: A dozen dancers in a black box theater. I cried in row two.

moments.title: Coffee in Greenpoint
moments.text: We talked about how weird it is that we both ended up here.

moments.title: Met at Musical
moments.transcript: Elise, the musical. She said paint it bigger, and I did.

name: Mohammed Rahman
story: Robotics teammate who is now a surgical resident in Boston. Still has the steadiest hands I know.

moments.title: Phone call
moments.text: On his way to a fourteen-hour shift and joking about it.

moments.title: Group video call
moments.text: Seven of us from the robotics club reuniting online.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Mo, the one who soldered with his tongue out. Dead steady.

name: Kelsey Moran
story: Edited the school paper and made me redraw a cartoon three times. Covers Congress now.

moments.title: Phone call
moments.text: She is on a deadline and called anyway to say hi.

moments.title: Visit in DC
moments.text: She showed me the press gallery and a very good sandwich.

moments.title: Met at School newspaper
moments.transcript: Kelsey, editor. She cut my caption to six words and was right.

name: Trent Callahan
story: Cross country teammate who now builds apartment buildings in Denver. Texts a photo every time he passes a trailhead.

moments.title: Group text
moments.text: A photo of his dog on a trail, with the caption you'd hate it.

moments.title: Wedding
moments.text: He caught the bouquet and refused to give it back.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Trent, the one who always forgot his shoes.

name: Sofia Bianchi
story: Worked the cafe next to the bookstore and traded me cookies for drawings. Pastry chef at a restaurant in Carroll Gardens now.

moments.title: Restaurant visit
moments.text: She sent out a dessert I didn't order and it was the best course.

moments.title: Surprise reunion
moments.text: We realized we live twelve blocks apart. She laughed for a full minute.

moments.title: Met at Bookstore job
moments.transcript: Sofia, from the cafe. Cookies for drawings was a fair trade.

name: Adam Brodsky
story: Lab partner who blew up one experiment on purpose. Teaches chemistry and homebrews.

moments.title: Homebrew night
moments.text: A stout that tasted like chocolate and regret.

moments.title: Zoom trivia
moments.text: His chemistry round was brutal.

moments.title: Met at Chemistry class
moments.transcript: Adam, lab partner. He said the smoke was supposed to do that.

name: Rebecca Lindgren
story: Played cello two chairs from me in orchestra. Delivers babies and still practices Bach on her night off.

moments.title: Quartet reunion
moments.text: Four of us played badly for two hours and loved it.

moments.title: Visit
moments.text: She told me about her hundredth birth, softly.

moments.title: Met at Orchestra
moments.transcript: Rebecca, cello. She taught me to tune by ear.

name: Isaiah Grant
story: Pickup basketball regular who never passed to me. Coaches the JV team and reformed his ways.

moments.title: JV game
moments.text: I sat behind the bench and shouted the wrong play.

moments.title: Backyard hoops
moments.text: Lost 21-3 and ate burgers.

moments.title: Met at Pickup games
moments.transcript: Isaiah, pickup. He told me to stop dribbling.

name: Valeria Santos
story: Art class friend who rearranged the classroom every month. Designs apartments in Brooklyn and moved my couch twice.

todos.text: Ask her about the bedroom layout

moments.title: Apartment visit
moments.text: She rearranged my living room in an hour and I haven't moved anything since.

moments.title: Brunch
moments.text: We figured out we shared a bus stop for six years.

moments.title: Met at Art class
moments.transcript: Valeria, art class. She said the room needed a diagonal.

name: Jun Ito
story: The runner who always had ginger candy. Pharmacist in the Bay now and still runs the Bay to Breakers.

todos.text: See him on the SF trip

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: He ran a half marathon in costume. A taco.

moments.title: Bay to Breakers
moments.text: I cheered from a curb and got a high five.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Jun, the ginger candy runner.

name: Tessa Wolfe
story: Volunteer partner at the food pantry. Now a social worker in Chicago who tells me to take a day off.

moments.title: Coffee
moments.text: She told me to log off for a weekend. I did, barely.

moments.title: Food drive
moments.text: We packed boxes together over video.

moments.title: Met at Volunteering
moments.transcript: Tessa, the pantry. She stacked cans like a Tetris champion.

name: Ricardo Mejia
story: The bookstore's weekend stockroom guy who cooked staff lunches. Runs a taqueria in Chicago.

moments.title: Taqueria visit
moments.text: He fed me until I couldn't speak.

moments.title: Opening day
moments.text: Hung his sign with a level.

moments.title: Met at Bookstore job
moments.transcript: Ricardo, stockroom. He made lunch for six every Saturday.

name: Monica Farrell
story: The guidance counselor who read my college essay four times. Still sends articles about design.

moments.title: Email
moments.text: She forwarded an article on design careers and a joke.

moments.title: Graduation party
moments.text: She gave me a mug that said you did it.

moments.title: Met at High school
moments.transcript: Ms. Farrell, counselor. She said apply to Michigan and stop doubting.

name: Lucas Ferrari
story: The programmer on the robotics team who moved to Toronto for hockey and tech. Plays on a beer league.

moments.title: Game night
moments.text: Four hours of a cooperative game. We lost heroically.

moments.title: Holiday call
moments.text: He sent a picture of his new puppy.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Lucas, the code guy.

name: Emilia Novak
story: Ran on the girls team and now works at an animal hospital in Madison. Sends cheese curds in the mail.

moments.title: Care package
moments.text: A box of cheese curds and a handwritten note.

moments.title: Zoom run
moments.text: Six of us ran in our own towns and compared splits.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Emilia, girls cross country.

name: Bruno Castro
story: Film club friend who shot our final movie on a camcorder. Films weddings and music videos in Los Angeles.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: He showed me a wedding film that made me tear up.

moments.title: LA trip
moments.text: He let me hold the boom pole on a shoot.

moments.title: Met at Film club
moments.transcript: Bruno, film club. He yelled action with real conviction.

name: Hana Schmidt
story: Robotics teammate who preferred plants to circuits. Designs gardens in Portland.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: She walked me through a rooftop garden she designed.

moments.title: Portland trip
moments.text: She showed me a native plant I couldn't pronounce.

moments.title: Met at Robotics club
moments.transcript: Hana, robotics. She named the robot Fern.

name: Dominic Russo
story: Mikey's older brother who coached the freshman runners. Now a police officer who volunteers at the track club.

moments.title: Track club
moments.text: He handed me a stopwatch and made me time the kids.

moments.title: Barbecue
moments.text: He grilled and told me I run like I'm late.

moments.title: Met at Cross country team
moments.transcript: Dominic, upperclassman. He gave me a pep talk before my first race.

name: Priya Menon
story: Science Olympiad partner who never lost a round. Researches cancer therapies in Cambridge.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: She explained her research in a way I almost understood.

moments.title: Group call
moments.text: A reunion of the Olympiad team over video.

moments.title: Met at Science Olympiad
moments.transcript: Priya, Science Olympiad. She quizzed me on bones in the car.

name: Zach Feldman
story: Wrote the school paper's tech column when I drew the comics. Covers startups for a magazine and lives in Williamsburg.

moments.title: Beers
moments.text: He asked what the next big design tool will be. I made it up.

moments.title: Moved to New York
moments.text: He texted that he'd found the same bagel place as me.

moments.title: Met at School newspaper
moments.transcript: Zach, the paper. He wrote an article about my doodles.

name: Alma Torres
story: Film club friend who produced everything. Produces documentaries in Brooklyn.

moments.title: Coffee
moments.text: She pitched me a doc about public libraries.

moments.title: Screening
moments.text: Sat in the back of her premiere.

moments.title: Met at Film club
moments.transcript: Alma, film club. She made a budget for a five-dollar movie.

name: Neil Banerjee
story: Lived across the hall freshman year and stayed up with me through every problem set. Now a consultant who flies out every Monday and lands back in Murray Hill on Thursday. Cooks elaborate dinners for six.

moments.title: Dinner at his place
moments.transcript: Six courses, none of which he had made before. We played a board game until two and he won by cheating.

moments.title: Rooftop birthday
moments.text: He had just moved to New York himself. Ten of us from Ann Arbor on one roof.

moments.title: Met at East Quad, freshman hall
moments.transcript: Neil, from the hall. Offered me half a pizza at 2am and has not stopped since.

name: Tomas Herrera
story: Down the hall from Neil and me. Studied mechanical engineering and now works on electric vehicles in Detroit. Hosts a tailgate for every Michigan home game and keeps a spare ticket for me.

todos.text: Go to the Ohio State tailgate
Ask what the team is building

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: He gave me the thirty-second version of his work on battery packs and then forty minutes on his chili recipe.

moments.title: Michigan football weekend
moments.text: We lost badly and ate chili in the parking lot anyway.

moments.title: Met at East Quad, freshman hall
moments.transcript: Tomas, the engineer on our floor. Had a poster of a car I could not name.

name: Keisha Williams
story: Our resident advisor freshman year. Gave me the first real talk about not skipping classes and the first real hug after a hard exam. Now writes tech policy in DC and still sends a calendar invite for my birthday.

todos.text: Ask for advice on an apartment lease dispute

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: She is up for a promotion at the policy institute. Told me to apply for the design lead role I was nervous about.

moments.title: Holiday party in DC
moments.text: Danced with everyone on our old hall. She remembered every middle name.

moments.title: Met at East Quad, resident advisor
moments.transcript: Keisha, our RA. She knocked on every door the first night and asked if we had eaten.

name: Eli Novak
story: Roommate in the house on Church Street senior year. Went from line cook to general manager of a restaurant group's flagship in Brooklyn. Cooks dinner for the whole building on Sundays.

todos.text: Ask about booking for my birthday

moments.title: Sunday dinner
moments.transcript: Nine people at his long table. He had put me next to a stylist who is now my friend.

moments.title: Restaurant opening
moments.text: He cried at the pass after the first service. I took the photo he later framed.

moments.title: Met at House on Church Street
moments.transcript: Eli, roommate. First thing he said: where do we keep the cast iron.

name: Bryn Abbott
story: Housemate who kept a tank of sea slugs in the kitchen. Now a marine biologist in Seattle who studies kelp. Knits hats for everyone she loves.

todos.text: Visit when the kelp survey is done

moments.title: Video call
moments.transcript: She was on a boat with spotty signal and showed me a kelp forest through the phone. It looked like a cathedral.

moments.title: Care package
moments.text: A knit hat with a tiny slug on it arrived a week into my first New York winter.

moments.title: Met at House on Church Street
moments.transcript: Bryn, the housemate with the tank. Warned me about the slugs.

name: Hiro Sato
story: Housemate and fellow design student. Moved to Toronto for a design job and then never left. Takes photos on a film camera and will make you try every cup of coffee he roasts.

moments.title: Design crit over video
moments.transcript: He gave me four honest notes on my case study, three of which stung. All four were right.

moments.title: Visited Toronto
moments.text: He showed me three coffee shops and one very good noodle counter. I bought a film camera.

moments.title: Met at House on Church Street
moments.transcript: Hiro, housemate. He had three monitors and one chair.

name: Dani Moreno
story: Housemate with the best taste of anyone I know. Became a high school art teacher in Los Angeles, thrifts every Sunday and has dressed me for three weddings. Mails a care package of vintage patches once a year.

todos.text: Ask her to shop for a jacket

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: She showed me a 1970s denim jacket she found for nine dollars. Sent me the link to the thrift store's tiny website.

moments.title: LA trip
moments.text: Spent a Sunday going through four thrift stores and a swap meet. I came home with a leather jacket.

moments.title: Met at House on Church Street
moments.transcript: Dani, housemate. She wore a different vintage jacket every day of our first month.

name: Alex Ferrante
story: Editor-in-chief when I joined as the staff illustrator. Now a national reporter who covers housing. Taught me that a good headline is a design problem.

moments.title: Dinner after a deadline
moments.transcript: He had just filed a story on rent regulation. Asked me to make a chart that does not lie.

moments.title: Welcome to New York
moments.text: He took me for a very long walk through his old beats and bought me a slice.

moments.title: Met at Student newspaper
moments.transcript: Alex, the editor who edited my first illustration into something readable.

name: Sunita Rao
story: Sports editor who made the whole section run on spreadsheets. Now a data journalist in DC and the only person I trust with a pivot table. Hosts an annual bracket pool.

todos.text: Ask her about a chart style guide

moments.title: Bracket pool
moments.transcript: She sent me the standings and a very kind email about my last-place finish.

moments.title: Video call
moments.text: The first remote hangout of the pandemic. We watched an empty arena on a stream together.

moments.title: Met at Student newspaper
moments.transcript: Sunita, sports. She argued with the editor over a comma and won.

name: Paul Everett
story: The paper's photo editor and the reason my layouts looked decent. Photo editor at a Chicago daily now. Bikes everywhere and keeps every contact sheet.

todos.text: Visit when I am in Chicago

moments.title: Phone call
moments.transcript: He told me about covering a flood and not sleeping for two days. Said the best photo was the one he did not take.

moments.title: Last print issue party
moments.text: We all signed a copy of the final front page.

moments.title: Met at Student newspaper
moments.transcript: Paul, photo desk. He cropped my illustration into a better one.

name: Lena Fischer
profession: Managing editor at a nonprofit newsroom
story: Copy chief who has never let a typo through. Moved to Astoria for a newsroom job the same summer I came to New York. We do the Sunday crossword over the phone.

todos.text: Ask her to proofread the case study

moments.title: Crossword call
moments.transcript: We finished it in forty minutes. She told me about a funder pulling out and what it means for the newsroom.

moments.title: First New York dinner
moments.text: She met me at the subway with a map of the five best bagel places.

moments.title: Met at Student newspaper
moments.transcript: Lena, copy desk. Corrected my spelling on the welcome sheet.

name: Jasper Quinn
